title: add vpc control plane terraform: multi-az subnets, interface endpoints, peering, route53
author: Evelyn Park
description:
Add Terraform modules and top-level wiring for provisioning a VPC-hosted Private Control Plane with multi-AZ private subnets, interface endpoints, security groups, cross-account peering, and Route53 private hosted zone peering. Motivation: enable safe, repeatable network provisioning for Private deployments (VPC mode) and provide upgrade hooks for the private-installer to create/modify networking resources during install/upgrade. This PR contains:
- new modules/network/vpc-control-plane: multi-az subnet layouts, configurable AZ count, CIDR allocation, tags
- modules/network/interface-endpoints: configurable interface endpoints (S3, ECR, KMS, secretsmanager, sts, redwood-controlplane-api) with security group rules and VPC endpoints policy where applicable
- modules/network/peering: cross-account peering with optional route propagation and importable peering acceptance
- modules/network/route53-peering: private hosted zone association and conditional forwarding configuration for cross-VPC DNS resolution
- top-level terragrunt/terraform integration for private-installer to call these modules during provision/upgrade
- docs/installer/vpc-control-plane.md: usage, required IAM permissions, rollback notes, and testing checklist
Implementation notes:
- Parameterization: AZ count, subnet sizing per az, endpoint list, and whether to create peering are configurable. Default is 3 AZs to match typical production installs but can be overridden for single-az test clusters.
- Backwards compatibility: terraform resources are organized to minimize destructive changes. When peering is enabled for an existing cluster, changes are additive by default. The module includes an opt-in 'replace_on_cidr_change' flag to surface any breaking behaviour to operators.
- Security: all interface endpoints are created with dedicated security groups; control plane SG is tightly scoped to endpoint SGs and peering CIDRs. Default egress/ingress policy follows least privilege for control-plane-to-internal-services flows.
- Observability/hook points: module emits outputs for created subnet IDs, endpoint IDs, peering connection ID, and hosted zone IDs so installer and Helm chart can wire Route53 and kubeconfig secrets.
Testing performed:
- terraform plan/apply in staging account (3-AZ) with peering to demo-customer-vpc; validated routing and DNS resolution (dig against private-hosted zone via peering).
- Terraform fmt and validate ran in CI. An initial fmt failure was fixed in a follow-up commit.
- Smoke deploy using private-installer v0.9.2 to a staging cluster; control plane registered and passed health checks.
Checklist:
- [x] Terraform modules implemented and documented
- [x] Parameterized AZ/subnet/endpoint options
- [x] CI fmt/validate passing
- [x] E2E staging validation completed
- [x] Release notes drafted
Migration/upgrade notes:
- Existing customers upgrading installer should run a plan in a maintenance window. Peering creation requires an explicit approve step if cross-account acceptance is enabled. Rollback is supported but operators should remove dependent Route53 associations before deleting peering links.
